title: What is a Convolutional Neural Network?
description: How convolutional, pooling and fully connected layers work together to turn images - and even text matrices - into predictions.
content:
**Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)** is a type of neural network designed to handle structured grid data, such as images. It consists of multiple layer types:
• Convolutional layers - apply kernels (filters) to the input to capture local structures, e.g. borders or textures.
• Pooling layers - downsample feature maps, reducing computational complexity and extracting the most important features.
• Fully connected layers - combine the extracted features and generate the outputs.

Typical computer vision applications:
• Object recognition
• Image segmentation
• Image classification

CNNs in NLP:
• Sentences or documents are usually represented as matrices, where each row corresponds to a token, typically represented as a dense vector (embedding).
• Filters capture local patterns (like n-grams) by sliding them over the input matrix.
• CNNs are effectively applied in sentiment analysis, text classification and semantic matching problems.
